0.long_answer: The BK virus small T antigen perturbs the normal control of the cell cycle by binding to protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A). PP2A is an important host cell enzyme involved in regulating various cellular processes, including the cell cycle. By interacting with PP2A, the small T antigen disrupts its phosphatase activity, which in turn leads to dysregulation of key signaling pathways controlling cell proliferation and survival. This disruption is thought to contribute to viral replication and may also play a role in oncogenic transformation.
